title: She was taken.
paragraphs:
Not by choice.
Not by desire.
Not by sin.
And the shame tried to write her story for her.

What do you do when something happened to you…
that you never chose?

What do you do when your life gets caught
in someone else’s fear…
someone else’s sin…
someone else’s compromise?

And maybe…
that’s where you are.

Abram—called by God, chosen, anointed—
still trembled in fear.

He looked at Sarah’s beauty…
and instead of trusting God,
he protected himself.

And it placed her
in another man’s house.

She didn’t flirt her way into the palace.
She didn’t scheme her way into power.
She was positioned there
by someone else’s fear.
And some of you know that pain.

You didn’t ask for that trauma.
You didn’t choose that situation.
You didn’t plan that betrayal.

But you’re the one carrying
the weight of it.

🔥 Genesis 12:17
“The Lord afflicted Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, Abram’s wife.”

God did not call her
Pharaoh’s woman.

God did not rename her
based on what happened.

And heaven refuses
to mislabel you.
Some scholars interpret this moment as a divine legal defense—God Himself stepping in to protect Sarah’s covenant identity before any violation could define her.

Before man could rewrite her identity,
God secured it.

Before culture could label her,
God spoke over her.

Before shame could settle in,
God moved.

What happened to you
is not what defines you.

Because the story doesn’t just expose pain—
it exposes us.

Moments where we chose safety over obedience.
Moments where we protected ourselves
at the cost of someone else.
Moments where fear spoke louder
than faith.

🔥 Proverbs 29:25
“The fear of man lays a snare, but whoever trusts in the Lord is safe.”

It traps.
It distorts.
It sacrifices others
on the altar of self-protection.
So now we stand in two places at once:

Some of us are Sarah—
wounded by what we didn’t choose.

Some of us are Abram—
haunted by what we did choose.
This is where the story explodes into the Gospel.

Because Sarah’s rescue points forward
to a greater rescue.
On the cross, Jesus was also “taken.”

He was stripped.
Mocked.
Publicly shamed.

🔥 Isaiah 53:5
“But He was pierced for our transgressions; He was crushed for our iniquities…”

Where Sarah was defended,
Jesus was condemned.

Where Sarah was protected,
Jesus was pierced.

So that everything that tries to define you—
your sin, your past, your trauma, your failure—
would lose its authority.

🔥 2 Corinthians 5:21
“For our sake He made Him to be sin who knew no sin, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.”

You are more sinful than you admit.
And more loved than you can imagine.
To the one carrying shame from what was done to you:

Jesus sees.
Jesus knows.
Jesus defends your dignity.
To the one carrying guilt from what you’ve done:

Jesus calls you.
Jesus invites you.
Jesus paid for it.
You don’t just admire this story.

Will you keep wearing
a name God never gave you?

Will you keep carrying
a shame Jesus already carried?

Will you keep hiding
when grace is calling you forward?

🔥 Romans 10:9
“If you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved.”

The shame.
The fear.
The guilt.
The silence.
He is not intimidated by your story.
If this stirred something in you…
If this pierced deeper than words…
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
